extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, patent analysts, policymakers, researchers and WIPO data users
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological notes for compiling, classifying and interpreting WIPO patent application and grant statistics (definitions of patent families, origin counting, resident vs non-resident shares, technology field mapping, data sources and caveats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent family is defined as patent applications interlinked by one or more of the following: priority claim, Patent Cooperation Treaty national phase entry, continuation, continuation-in-part, internal priority, and addition or division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent families here include only those families associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude those associated with utility model applications. (Source: WIPO Statistics Database and EPO PATSTAT database, August 2024.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-oriented patent family definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A special subset of patent families comprises foreign-oriented patent families. This includes only patent families that have at least one filing office different from the office of the applicant’s country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some foreign-oriented patent families include only one filing office, because applicants may choose to file directly with a foreign office. Example: if a Canadian applicant files directly with the USPTO without previously filing in Canada, that application and subsequent USPTO filings form a foreign-oriented family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin determination (first-named applicant residence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a patent application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Origin data are based on absolute counts. For an absolute count, applications filed at regional offices are counted once, rather than being considered equivalent to multiple applications in the respective member states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute-count treatment of regional office filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For an absolute count, applications filed at regional offices are counted once, rather than being considered equivalent to multiple applications in the respective member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This counting method applies to origin data and patent grants when origin/grant statistics are reported (regional office grants/applications are not multiplied across member states).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident versus non-resident breakdown and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures showing total growth or decrease are broken down by the respective contributions of resident and non-resident applications (or grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreting the breakdown: e.g., applications at the IP office of the Islamic Republic of Iran grew by 2%; growth in resident applications accounted for 2.7 percentage points of this increase, while non-resident applications decreased by 0.7 percentage points. Use percentage-point contributions to attribute total growth to resident/non-resident components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published-application timing (18-month publication lag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published patent applications. There is a minimum 18-month delay between application date and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published application counts reflect this delay; users should account for publication lag when interpreting recent-year application totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution: do not compare applications and grants in same year
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for issuing patents varies between offices, and the examination process can take a long time, therefore there is invariably a time lag between application and grant dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this reason, data on applications for a given year should not be compared with data on grants for that same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation in issuance procedures across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for issuing patents varies between offices, and differences in the number of patents granted among offices depend on factors such as examination capacity and procedural delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences in grants across offices may reflect procedural capacity and delays rather than underlying inventive activity; interpret cross-office comparisons with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IPC technology concordance to map fields
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table was used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an electronic version of the IPC technology concordance table, visit www.wipo.int/en/web/ip-statistics. The concordance underpins field-of-technology distributions reported throughout the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: IPC-to-technology mapping is imperfect (no one-to-one correspondence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence between International Patent Classification (IPC) symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one-to-one correspondence). It is therefore difficult to capture all patents within a specific technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite mapping limitations, IPC-based definitions are likely to capture the vast majority of patent applications in a given technology area. For small, narrowly defined technologies (e.g., specific energy subfields) some patents may be missed; see annex A for definitions of specific technologies (fuel cell, geothermal, solar, wind, hydro).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of utility model applications from patent-family counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families here include only those families associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude those associated with utility model applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users interested in utility models must consult separate tables or data; family-based indicators in this report focus on invention patent applications only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for featured offices and origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Top offices and origins (e.g., 'top five offices', 'top 20 offices and origins') were selected based on their 2023 totals or on available 2023 data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected offices are drawn from different world regions; selection is driven by available 2023 data and totals rather than an exhaustive global list (see table references such as A60/A61 for fuller office coverage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and vintage
rubrics_metrics.description: Source: WIPO Statistics Database and EPO PATSTAT database, August 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures/tables use these source databases and the specified vintage; users should cite these sources and the vintage when reproducing or comparing figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy-technology definition and capture difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: For definitions of the technologies – fuel cell, geothermal, solar, wind and hydro energy – see annex A. The correspondence between IPC symbols and technology fields is not always apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is difficult to capture all patents within these five technology areas using IPC codes alone, but IPC-based definitions likely capture the vast majority. Users should be aware of this limitation when analyzing trends in energy-related patenting.
